verdicts.decision_note: The client establishes software-independent product acceptance behavior requiring a drip-free valve and a sealed spout connection that prevents liquid from entering the base.
The client extends liquid-containment behavior to the bowl seal and explicitly requires protection of electrical components; no existing attribute becomes obsolete.

The client requires physical separation between liquids and electrical components and applies that containment behavior to sanitation and potential retail-use contexts; no prior key conflicts with the added rule.
First concrete runtime failure: testing exposed an actual leak in the machine plumbing.
Target-specific post-failure implementation claim: the freelancer reports that the plumbing associated with the identified leak has been fixed, without yet providing runtime verification.
